description: Public-tree forbidden-pattern and secret-shape database for scripts/oss/check-public-tree.mjs. It contains only generic, non-sensitive path and content shapes: the forms a repository must never carry, independent of any one project's infrastructure. Exact environment-specific identifiers are deliberately not stored in this repository, in plaintext or in any encoded form - base64 is a reversible encoding, not a redaction, and the scanner rejects encoded pattern fields outright. Per-deployment baselines are validated during private release preparation, outside the tree. Exceptions are precise per-pattern path allowlists only - there is no global ignore and no self-exemption: this file and the scanner are scanned like every other file.
allowlistPolicy: Every allow entry is a file that has to contain a live-shaped value in order to prove something about itself: the notification redactors and their tests (private-key / AWS / OpenAI / bearer shapes), the frozen Admin device-receipt fixtures and the relay clients that verify them (PromptDock token shape), the generated pnpm lockfile (upstream registry metadata we do not author), and the desktop path-handling tests that pass a synthetic absolute path through the code under test. An allowlist for one detector never disables the other detectors for that file. Where a generic detector needs an exception, the narrowest possible one is used - never a whole detector class or directory.

pathPatterns.description: A working directory for audit or extraction evidence must not be published.
Pre-design comparison assets are not published.
A dated acceptance and evidence directory is not published.
Superseded internal archive docs are not published.
Internal evidence docs are not published.
Private key, keystore or DPAPI-encrypted credential material.
A directory named for secret storage is never published, whatever it holds.
Runtime database file: real schema and user data, never source.
Captured run log or trace: evidence that can carry request/response data.
Environment file with live values; only .env.example may be tracked.

contentPatterns.description: An absolute path rooted in a developer machine layout: a personal home, workspace or project directory.
contentPatterns.note: Shape-based, so it names no machine. Every one of the 15 lines it reported on first run was triaged: each holds a placeholder account name (example, test, someone, a CJK probe name) inside a fixture whose purpose is to be handed an absolute path. Those eight files are allowed by name; the detector stays on for the other 772.

contentPatterns.description: A per-user home directory path on a unix or macOS workstation, not a service account path a deployment would ship.
A bare IPv4 literal outside the loopback, private, link-local, shared, benchmarking and documentation ranges - a deployment address rather than an example.
contentPatterns.note: The guards carry the meaning and each has a case in scripts/oss/selftest-check-public-tree.mjs: the leading class rejects a letter or dot in front, so a tagged version reads as a version; the trailing pair rejects a further digit or a further octet, so 1.2.3.4.5 is a version while an address that ends a sentence is still an address.

contentPatterns.description: Email address that is not a reserved placeholder domain.
contentPatterns.note: weixin.qq.com is a public third-party service domain that appears as URL userinfo in endpoint-parsing tests, never as a person's mailbox.
